content.content:
License check, applied to the recorded dependent against the recorded prerequisite, both read as they stand.

Procedure. Read the dependent clause by clause: take each element it states — its condition or trigger, its subject, and each obligation or prohibition it adds, including everything it says about what happens when the root it names cannot be found — and locate the element of the prerequisite that clause rests on. Compare the two.

Failure. The check fails on the first dependent element that contradicts a stated element of the prerequisite. A clause that permits, requires or guarantees something a prerequisite element forecloses contradicts it, and so does a clause that states the opposite arrangement, the opposite source, or the opposite outcome; name the offending element and the prerequisite element it contradicts in the finding.

Pass. The check passes when no element of the dependent contradicts a stated element of the prerequisite. Silence in the prerequisite is not a failure, narrowing an element the prerequisite states is not a failure, and nothing beyond contradiction is examined: no traceability of clauses, no vocabulary, no wording match, no runnable behavior.

Application. A reviewer reads both recorded documents and reports the finding by element; there is no command to run and no fixture, and the criterion is decidable from the two node documents alone.
content.rationale:
Why this form: the prerequisite states its arrangement in prose, and the dependent is an EARS requirement — a requirement sentence, which the ladder treats as constrained notation, not prose-like free text. The matrix cell is therefore parent natural, child structured (natural-to-structured), whose form is the gate: a non-violation review of the elaboration against its parent, with no behavior probe. A test is not available and not permitted here — a requirement sentence is still words, and demanding observables of it would be the strictness the cell forbids.

Why this check: an elaboration of a prose prerequisite can go wrong in exactly one way — a clause that contradicts a clause of the parent — so a clause-by-clause license check is the whole of the gate, no more and no less. The load-bearing clause in this edge is the parent's prohibition on falling back to the invocation workspace's root when the trunk's state root cannot be resolved; the criterion covers it by treating the parent's prohibitions as stated elements, so a dependent clause that admits such a fallback contradicts the parent rather than extending it.

Independence and groundedness: the criterion names no element of either document in advance and quotes no wording, so an element it finds at check time is a finding, not part of what is recorded; rewriting the requirement without changing what it decides leaves the gate intact. Every rule it applies is stated by this edge — non-contradiction — and it presupposes no decision beyond the dependent and its recorded prerequisite.
